name: The Deccan Famine
historicalContext: Severe drought across the Deccan Plateau. Maharashtra declared famine conditions. 25 million people affected. Massive cattle death. Government launched Employment Guarantee Scheme (precursor to MGNREGA).

availableCrops.name: Jowar (Sorghum)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Staple food of the Deccan. Maharashtra's primary kharif crop. Survives on stored soil moisture alone.

availableCrops.name: Bajra (Pearl Millet)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Grown on marginal black-cotton soils of Vidarbha. Critical backup when jowar fails.

availableCrops.name: Tur Dal (Pigeon Pea)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Nitrogen-fixing legume. Improves soil health. Traditional intercrop with jowar in the Deccan system.

availableCrops.name: Groundnut
availableCrops.historicalNote: Cash crop of Marathwada. Needs timely rain at pegging stage. Total failure in 1972 drought.

availableCrops.name: Cotton (Desi)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Vidarbha's cotton belt. High water demand made it devastating during the drought. Many cotton farmers lost everything.

availableCrops.name: Hybrid Paddy
availableCrops.historicalNote: Attempted in canal-irrigated patches. Catastrophic failure when canals dried up. Wasted precious resources.

disaster.name: Groundwater Collapse & Cattle Death — भूजल संकट
disaster.triggerDescription: Wells across the Deccan run dry. Bore wells fail at 200ft depth. Cattle begin dying of thirst and starvation. Migration columns form on highways.

specialRules: Cattle need 2 fodder + 1 water per minute or lose 15 health/min
If cattle die, plot preparation takes 2x longer (no bullocks for plowing)
Each well pump costs 2x normal water
30% chance of salinization per excess pump cycle
Jowar+Tur intercrop combo gives +20% yield bonus
